given: a stock record that has been migrated up to first-class batch_number and serial_number columns with the combined column dropped
then: a combined inventory_code is reconstructed from the canonical location plus the split-out batch and serial, and the combined column is restored

independence.rationale: Prior ACs cover the forward migration and reporting; AC6 covers the reverse path. The up migration could be entirely correct while the down path is missing or reconstructs the code wrongly, so reversibility breaks independently.

architectural_notes: Infra. The down revision re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs it from canonical location + batch + serial (PI1 migration_reversible, NFR-F6-reversibility). Reconstruction is lossy only for nonconforming rows whose batch/serial are NULL, so the round-trip assertion covers conforming rows. MUST be a kind:fitness test marked @pytest.mark.migration on an ISOLATED ephemeral Lakebase branch (apply up -> alembic downgrade -1 -> assert inventory_code restored), NEVER on the shared verify branch: downgrading the shared branch would drop batch_number/serial_number and re-add inventory_code, breaking every UP-state test (AC1-AC5). This same isolated fitness test also carries PI1 and the whole-row survival check for PI4 (AC1/AC2 second clause). Cross-cutting: reversibility is a migration/Infra guarantee defended by the migration fitness function, isolated from the shared-branch behavior suite.
